notes: The session's web-search allowance ran out after the first six candidates (thirteen searches), so the rest were researched by reading pages directly: the candidates' own sites, government sites, party units' sites and a few named news sites, always with the kit's honest User-Agent and each site's robots.txt obeyed. No search engine was read in place of the search tool.

The campaign websites the candidates filed were learned by running the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) on a scratch copy of the database; each was then opened and read. Four more campaign sites were found another way and read: Bob Sullentrop's (linked from the Minneapolis Republican Party's site), Mike Hang's (linked from the Senate District 44 DFL's page of endorsed candidates), and Christine Scherbing's and Ann Miller's (by asking whether the likely address exists, then reading the site; each names the candidate, the office and 2026).

Not read, and nothing worked around: the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (a Cloudflare check), the state's mn.gov pages (a Radware CAPTCHA), Karen A. Larson's filed campaign site (a bot check), the Swift County and City of Detroit Lakes sites (their robots.txt asks scripts to stay out), the Forum Communications newspapers (their robots.txt turns Claude away).
Nothing was found for six candidates: Gary Spatenka, Tom Walsh, Thomas R. Klyve, Patrick Allan Voss, Chuck Kobes and Mike Cross. They are listed with no findings.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape part 10 uses): Joe Scott is named by the Carver County Republican Party under 'Recommended Candidates', a heading that is not the word endorsement, so it is kept apart from endorsed_by and no page should call it an endorsement; whether and how it is shown is John's decision.

Jonathan Claussen: KAXE reports that Republican delegates endorsed him, and his own site says so, but no party page that says endorsed was found (the Wadena County and Todd County Republicans list him as a candidate), so there is no endorsed_by entry for him.
Ages stated without a year were not turned into birth years (KAXE gives Jonathan Claussen's age on Election Day; Ngone Niang's and Jess Garcia's own sites give an age).

verifier_notes: Every address in the file was opened again on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent; all answered, none showed a wall.

Duane Quam's review item was checked against state_mn.sqlite (two terms: 25A with no start date ending 2023-01-02, and 24A from 2023-01-03) and against the Legislative Reference Library's record, which reads House 2011-2012 (29A), 2013-2022 (25A), 2023-Present (24A).
Bob Sullentrop's birth year comes from a secondary source that gives a full date; only the year is kept, as the rules require.

Ngone Niang's endorsement is the Green Party of Minnesota's own release, carried on the national Green Party's site (gp.org), not on the state party's own site; it is kept as a party's own page, and John may wish to know where it sits.
Joe Scott's party_support entry was confirmed as worded ('Recommended Candidates', not 'Endorsed') and stays apart from endorsed_by.
